cadence.task: Review open MaintainX work orders and critical equipment issues
Review due/overdue PMs; confirm dish, smart oven, grounds and weekly equipment PMs
Reconcile MaintainX with PM calendar; complete filters, gaskets, safety checks and facility inspections
Coordinate HVAC/refrigeration coils, belts, vendor PMs, grease/fire/hood items and repeat-failure review
HVAC seasonal startups, grounds/winterization, regulatory/vendor annual inspections and asset review

steps.title: 1. Asset Setup
steps.text: Every major piece of kitchen, refrigeration, dish, facility, grounds, and service equipment that needs tracked gets a permanent Asset ID. I match that Asset ID to the MaintainX asset whenever possible.

steps.title: 2. PM Setup
steps.text: Each asset that requires preventive maintenance gets a PM frequency, task description, responsible person or vendor, and due date. MaintainX handles the live reminders. The PM Master Schedule is the backup.

steps.title: 3. Completing a PM
steps.text: The person completing the PM checks the full task list, records anything found, and does not mark the PM complete until the required work is finished or a separate work order has been created for anything that still needs attention.

steps.title: 4. Problems Found During PM
steps.text: If a PM inspection finds a repair issue, I create a work order in MaintainX and assign the correct priority. I record major repairs, costs, downtime, and repeat problems in the Work Order History sheet.

steps.title: 5. Safety / Food Safety Issues
steps.text: Anything that could affect employee safety, fire safety, food safety, refrigeration temperatures, sanitation, or normal restaurant operation gets escalated immediately. The equipment is taken out of service when necessary.

steps.title: 6. Vendor Service
steps.text: When outside service is required, I record the vendor, service date, work performed, parts replaced, cost when available, and any follow-up recommendation. Important service paperwork should be kept with the maintenance records.

steps.title: 7. PM Backup Review
steps.text: I update the spreadsheet backup from MaintainX on a regular basis. At minimum, I check completed PMs, upcoming due dates, overdue items, major repairs, and open work orders.

steps.title: 8. Repeat Failures
steps.text: If the same asset keeps breaking down, I flag it for review instead of treating every work order as a separate problem. Repair frequency, downtime, and total cost should be considered before more money is put into the equipment.

steps.title: 9. Equipment Replacement
steps.text: When repair cost, reliability, food-safety risk, or downtime becomes unreasonable, I document the issue and bring a replacement recommendation to management with the repair history to back it up.

steps.title: 10. Record Retention
steps.text: MaintainX remains the live record. The workbook is the backup and long-term reference. Major invoices, service reports, warranty information, and inspection records should be kept where they can be matched back to the Asset ID.

priorities.use: Immediate safety, food-safety, refrigeration, fire, or critical operational issue.
Major operational impact but the restaurant can continue operating.
Repair is needed but there is limited operational impact.

priorities.response: Complete as time and budget allow.
